content.comment_body: I have a [product_name] and have been trying to connect it to the cloud for two days, but have not been successful. I've closely followed multiple support threads, reviewed issues others have had—mostly related to subnet mismatches—and I believe my configuration is correct, but I still can't connect to the cloud. I repeatedly see a 'DNS server is not available' error when testing the connection. I've registered my device as a thing on AWS (using the same location settings, though I'm in Australia), and can see the thing in my AWS account, but the test connection fails in [product_name] software. I decided to focus on just the local connections to see if it's a local issue. Here are my IP addresses: - Device: 10.0.0.5 (gateway: 10.0.0.138) - PC Ethernet Card: 10.0.0.1 (gateway: 10.0.0.138) The network scan shows all devices on 10.0.0.xx, with the router at 10.0.0.138 and my device at 10.0.0.5. Connections: - PC Ethernet is connected to the router - Device is connected to the router I can ping the device from the PC without any issues, and IP config looks correct. However, when I try to connect within [product_name] software, I get a subnet error, even though both devices are on the same subnet and can ping each other. If I confirm the prompt from the software, it adds another subnet IP to my Ethernet card—though this seems unnecessary as the card already has a subnet IP. The connection still fails afterward. Interestingly, if I remove the router and directly connect PC to device via Ethernet, the connection works, suggesting an issue with the router or its settings. I've also tried using my PC's wifi together with a wired PC-to-device connection, which works for local communication between the device and software, but I still can't connect to the cloud. I've tried setting a manual IP on my Ethernet card and using DNS 8.8.8.8, but this also fails. Any advice would be greatly appreciated! Thank you
Hi, If you are unable to establish a cloud connection using the application example "[product_name] - Connection to a cloud," it's best to reach out to Technical Support. Best regards, [user_name]
Thank you for the suggestion, [user_name]. I'll review the link!

analysis.insight_summary: The user is experiencing ongoing issues when trying to connect a [product_name] to the cloud with [product_name] software, including DNS and subnet errors. Attempts to follow troubleshooting guides and configuration steps have not resolved the issue. Local network connectivity works, but cloud connectivity remains unreachable. Ambiguous software feedback during the setup process is a major source of frustration, hindering effective problem-solving.
analysis.user_expectations: The user expects an easy cloud setup, clear diagnostics, and straightforward troubleshooting when linking devices to cloud services. Reliable connectivity and informative software error messages are anticipated for quick and successful setup.
